chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "How will you be when your women become corrupt and your youth become dissolute, and you do not enjoin what is right and do not forbid what is wrong?"
It was said to him, "And will that happen, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Yes, and something worse than that. How will you be when you enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right?"
It was said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, and will that happen?" He said, "Yes, and something worse than that. How will you be when you see what is right as wrong, and what is wrong as right?"
ai.seo_question: What are the stages of moral decline described in this hadith regarding enjoining good and forbidding evil?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines a three-stage degeneration of societal morality, culminating in the inversion of values where the good is perceived as evil and vice versa, a state often associated with the era of the Major Occultation. Shia scholars emphasize this progression as a diagnostic tool for assessing the spiritual health of the community, linking the failure of *Amr bi-l-Ma'ruf* to the eventual loss of divine guidance. The narration serves as a warning that moral relativism precedes comprehensive collapse, urging believers to maintain clear discernment (*furqan*) amidst changing norms.
